front:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Produce ONE clean FRONT ORTHOGRAPHIC full-body A-pose model reference of the baseline worker robot for the existing game Loopforge. This is image-to-3D input, not a scene or collage. Portrait 2:3 composition, single robot occupying most of height, entire head, fingers and soles visible, ample silhouette margin, plain light neutral grey background, no ground plane, no cast shadow, no labels/text/watermark. Camera straight-on at mid-body height, zero perspective foreshortening. Quiet neutral studio lighting with enough fill to clearly see all construction and surfaces. Sharp, highly resolved, materially believable dark industrial illustration with the gritty fine painted detail of the reference art; NOT cartoon/toy, not a glossy new sci-fi soldier.
REFERENCE IMAGE 1 limen_security: use the SMALL WORKER waiting with paperwork behind LIMEN at image x~690 y~360 for head identity: squat fitted metal cranial cap with subtle center seam, two separate round cyan glass optics in protective goggle rings, inset brow band, circular ear bearings and narrow vertical ventilation grille mouth. Do NOT copy the huge skull-faced armoured LIMEN in foreground, weapons, nameplates or scene. Expression unassuming, slightly blank. Normal adult proportions ~7.5 heads tall; eyes bright but modest with no bloom haze.
REFERENCE IMAGE 2 thrum_conveyor: use the ordinary worker at the far RIGHT for body identity, NOT Thrum with boombox head. Lean but sturdy factory labourer; shaped worn charcoal/green-grey steel chest assembly, rectangular recessed sternum service plate, ribbed narrow articulated abdomen, coherent pelvis chassis, modest fitted curved shoulder shells over recessed joints, tapered forearms and shins, segmented mechanical thighs, honest load-bearing rods and cylindrical hinge bearings, five-finger articulated hands with thumbs, planted split-toe industrial feet. Strong continuous mechanical anatomy rather than balls/capsules. Smaller and considerably less ornate than a supervisor, utilitarian not heroic armour.
MATERIALS: rubbed gunmetal edges, chipped faded dark petrol enamel on shaped panels, occasional tarnished brass fasteners, oily recesses, restrained surface scratches and subtle tool marks, believable clear separation of enamel/metal/rubber. A few quiet broad surfaces so shape reads at a small camera size. No fabric/cloak/loose hoses/pouches/attached tools. Tiny restrained cyan eyes only; no bright chest core or glowing limb strips. No text anywhere.
POSE: symmetrical clean relaxed A-pose: straight spine, head level looking forward; arms straight and angled down 40 degrees from horizontal, palms facing forward, all five fingers gently separated visibly, hands well clear of torso/thighs. Feet flat, parallel, hip-width apart; legs straight with a gap, no crouch or contrapposto. Fingers thin enough to articulate but mechanically sturdy. Make joint centres and clearance convincing. Both hands empty. No machine/workpiece/prop/scenery.
This FRONT view is the master identity for subsequent side/back views. Prioritize exact readable mechanical form, faithful worker head design and riggable anatomical separation over atmospheric beauty.

backCorrection:

Second reference image is the true SIDE of this SAME robot and clarifies correct foot depth and body construction. Keep the EXACT silhouette, dimensions, A-pose, head back, shoulders and overall industrial material palette of image 1. Correct it into a genuine anatomically credible rear view. CRITICAL FOOT CORRECTION: We are looking at the BACK OF THE HEELS, with the toes pointing AWAY from the camera and mostly occluded by each heel/shin. Remove those split toe boxes pointing at us! The visible closest surface of each foot is a solid short heel block, shallow horizontal rubber sole, a vertical rear heel cap and Achilles-like vertical ankle piston above it. The tips of toes cannot appear in front of these heels. This must unambiguously look like two HEELS.
CRITICAL LEGS: back of shin has protected slender actuator and recessed rear calf service slot instead of the front broad shin plate. Back of knee shows bent linkage recess, NOT a square kneecap. Rear thighs have plainer curved panels and tendon-like protected rods, not mirrored forward-facing thigh plates. A compact coherent rear pelvis with horizontal access cover, not a pointed front codpiece. Same hip width and proportions.
CRITICAL HANDS: seeing PALMS because the original front pose showed dorsal mechanical knuckles; hands must have palm pads/linkages rather than duplicate knuckle plates. Thumb placement must be geometrically correct for the SAME pose viewed from behind: thumbs on the INWARD sides of hands, toward body's midline, four long fingers outward from those thumbs. Arms are straight in the SAME downward A-pose.
BACK/TORSO: keep compact fitted rear maintenance cover with a narrow vertical vent at center, enclosed spine with small articulated rear vertebra covers, restrained protected cables. Do not mirror the front chest's horizontal display recess. Do not add a giant backpack.
Preserve worn charcoal/petrol steel, tarnished brass fasteners, normal adult proportions, gritty realistic Loopforge robot style. No new appendages, props, text, emissive back eyes, shoulder spikes, platform or ground shadow. Accurate back anatomy is the purpose of this correction.
